rows.grounds: dvandva compound in genitive dual naming the northeast and east directions
locative form indicating the position between the two named directions
qualifies the fire-pit as the main one
compound of vṛtta and kuṇḍaka denoting a circular fire-pit

items.question: Which fire-pit holds the principal position between Īśāna and Indra among the directional fire-pits?
premises: Fire-pits are arranged around the platform in the eight directions.
The space between Īśāna and Indra is a specified location.
A round fire-pit is designated as principal in that location.
items.inference: The principal fire-pit among the directional arrangements is the round one placed between Īśāna and Indra.
uncertainties: The exact directional identification of śakra as east is assumed from standard convention.
items.plain_english: Between Īśāna and Indra, one should place the principal round fire-pit.
